test-chem-a:
You are writing full-length unit tests for an AP Chemistry study app — the kind of test a strong AP teacher gives at the end of a unit, where every question makes the student think. You are writing the tests for units u1, u2, u3 of the course "chem" (unit "x" is the Connections unit: its test is a cumulative exam across the whole course).

Read {GEN}/SPEC-test.md in full — it is the brief, and its one rule is that every question is critical thinking: no question a student could answer from memory alone. Also read the house style for math in {GEN}/SPEC.md (the "Exclusions, borrowing, style" section) and the checker {GEN}/tests.py.

Chemistry: a teacher's unit test leans on lab work and data — an experiment whose procedure has a flaw and the question of which way it moves the result; a data table that supports one conclusion and not another; a particulate diagram described in words; a student's claim to evaluate; a prediction paired with its reason. Give every constant a question needs (R, molar masses, K values, E° values); students have the AP equation sheet and a periodic table. Compute every number, including each distractor's slip, with python.

For each unit, load {GEN}/in/chem-<unit>.json with python for the CED topics, LOs, EK statements, exclusions and skills, and load {GEN}/out/chem-<unit>.json to see the existing multiple-choice sets and free-response questions (print one of each; never print a whole file) so you match the house style and do not repeat them. The course's topic codes and skill codes are in /home/user/JuniorYearFlashcardsApp/data/chem.json (units[].topics[].c, skills[].code).

Write the tests one unit at a time, in the order given. For each, build it in {GEN}/out/test-chem-<unit>.py (a python script that writes {GEN}/out/test-chem-<unit>.json), adding one group at a time and re-running the script after each, so an interruption loses little. If a script already exists, read it, check it, and continue where it stops. Run `python3 {GEN}/tests.py check chem <unit>` until it prints RESULT PASS with no warnings. Then re-read every question as a student would see it and fix anything ambiguous, anything with two defensible answers, and anything a student could answer without thinking.

Write only {GEN}/out/test-chem-u1.json and {GEN}/out/test-chem-u2.json and {GEN}/out/test-chem-u3.json and their .py scripts. Do not write anything else under {GEN}/out/, and nothing under /home/user/JuniorYearFlashcardsApp.

When you finish, reply with, for each test: the checker's summary line, its groups with their stimulus kinds in a few words, its free-response titles, and anything you were unsure of. Nothing else.
